subject.title: fix #95351: [Feature]: Generic JSONL line-parsing hook for CliBackendPlugin (native tool-card support beyond claude-stream-json)

question: Should OpenClaw commit to `CliBackendPlugin.parseJsonlEvent` and its six-event normalized JSONL union as a supported public plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The implementation creates an opt-in but durable external API; tests can validate mechanics but cannot decide whether this is the intended long-term plugin boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the public JSONL hook
options.body: Accept the hook as the canonical plugin-owned parser seam, then require current-head installed-plugin subprocess proof and focused compatibility coverage before merge.

options.title: Reject the new SDK surface
options.body: Keep the existing CLI backend contract unchanged and route any provider-specific integration through an external package only if it can use current supported seams.

options.title: Request a narrower contract design
options.body: Pause this branch while owners define a smaller or more general plugin event boundary with explicit compatibility and ownership documentation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the public JSONL hook
recommendation.body: Accept the hook as the canonical plugin-owned parser seam, then require current-head installed-plugin subprocess proof and focused compatibility coverage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline routed the current SDK-direction decision to this person; feature-history ownership could not be independently corroborated from the available read-only inspection.
